LESSON: READING ALOUD (FLUENCY)

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.5 Reading Aloud (fluency) (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, t
Topic 2.7: Reading aloud (Fluency)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading aloud (Fluency), part of Reading 2.5 Reading Aloud (fluency) (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, t in Grade 7 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: How can we improve our fluency in a language?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify sound patterns in reading for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading aloud (Fluency) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read texts aloud for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading aloud (Fluency) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate role of reading aloud in fluency.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading aloud (Fluency) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify sound patterns in reading for fluency,

   Reading aloud (Fluency) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read texts aloud for fluency,

   Reading aloud (Fluency) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate role of reading aloud in fluency.

   Reading aloud (Fluency) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read descriptions of people and underline the adjectives used,

2. read descriptions of people and match them to the given pictures,

3. read aloud presentations describing their favourite people by their appearances and personality using adjectives such as nett, freundlich, groβ usw,

4. discuss in plenary the appropriate ways of describing one’s physical appearance.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read descriptions of people and underline the adjectives used,
2. read descriptions of people and match them to the given pictures,
3. read aloud presentations describing their favourite people by their appearances and personality using adjectives such as nett, freundlich, groβ usw,
4. discuss in plenary the appropriate ways of describing one’s physical appearance.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading aloud (Fluency) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: the learner develops skills of speaking clearly and effectively as they read aloud

presentations describing the appearance and personality of their favourite people using adjectives such as nett, freundlich,

groβ usw.

• Self-efficacy: the learner develops effective communication skills as they read aloud presentations describing their favourite

people by their appearances using adjectives such as nett, freundlich, groβ usw.
